note: Two X posts captured on the morning of 18 August 2026. One reports a settled round 1; the other is a round 2 forecast made before round 2 was played, so git history is the evidence it predates the football.

whyThisFileMattersMoreThanItsContents.what: The round-1 screenshot is what exposed a fault in this project's OWN published record.
whyThisFileMattersMoreThanItsContents.how: It shows real Fantasy EFL round-1 scores as small positive integers — 2, 12, 3, 8, 5, 15, 6 — against a stated GW1 average of 44 and a squad total of 54. Our ledger had graded the same round with every one of 3,442 players on roughly minus two hundred and fifty points and our squad on -1899.
whyThisFileMattersMoreThanItsContents.outcome: The grading was diagnosed as a season-rollover subtraction, voided, and a guard added so it cannot publish again. See voidedGrading in efl/data/rounds/round-01.json.
whyThisFileMattersMoreThanItsContents.theUncomfortablePart: Nothing inside this project caught it. The ledger graded, committed and published a round that describes nothing, and the model's rank correlation was published at -0.718 as though it were a verdict on the model. It took a stranger's screenshot.

observedRoundOneScores.provenance: Read off @FEFLFinny's own squad screenshot. These are ANOTHER MANAGER'S players, not ours, and the value here is the SCALE of Fantasy EFL round-1 scoring, not the individual picks.
observedRoundOneScores.twoFurtherPlayersNotFullyVisible: The screenshot cuts off below the front two, showing two more shirts (Leicester City and one other) without their scores. Seven of a seven-player squad are named in the visible rows, so the cut-off shirts are presumably the bench or a larger squad than our rules model — either way they are NOT transcribed, because a number that cannot be read is not a number.
observedRoundOneScores.whatThisEstablishes: Round-1 Fantasy EFL scores are single- and low-double-digit positive integers, and a seven-player squad averages 44. Any grading that puts a squad at -1899 is measuring something else.

gradesSomethingWeAlreadyHeld.caution: Three points is one round. This is recorded as the first data point against a pre-round pick, not as a verdict on the source.

roundTwoForecast.howItGrades: Club points for Luton and Fleetwood in round 2, on the same basis the ledger uses for our own club picks — once the ledger can grade again.
roundTwoForecast.checkableFactsInsideIt: Every stated reason is a checkable claim about results — Luton's margin at Reading, Notts County's goals in six, Fleetwood's eight-match record, Gillingham's goal difference. NONE of them has been checked here: the Fantasy EFL feed is unreachable from this sandbox (the egress proxy refuses gameweekedge.co.uk), so they are transcribed and left unverified rather than assumed.

oneThingItSaysAboutOurOwnRoundOne.what: The Luton post states a '4-goal away win against Reading'.
oneThingItSaysAboutOurOwnRoundOne.whyItIsRelevant: Reading was one of this project's two club picks for round 1.
oneThingItSaysAboutOurOwnRoundOne.whatItImplies: Reading conceded at least four at home in the round we backed them. That is consistent with a poor club return.
oneThingItSaysAboutOurOwnRoundOne.whyItIsNotRecordedAsAResult: It is a passing clause in a third party's promotional post, not a result table, and 'a 4-goal away win' is ambiguous between a 4-0 scoreline and a four-goal margin. The ledger will grade our club picks from the feed when it can grade again. This is a pointer, not a number.

whatCannotBeSettledFromHere: Our own round-1 squad and club points. The feed is unreachable from this sandbox and the lock baseline is unusable across the season rollover. Round 1 is UNGRADED and is recorded as ungraded — not zero, not estimated, and not backfilled from a screenshot of somebody else's team.
Every factual claim inside the round-2 forecast, for the same reason.
Whether the two cut-off shirts in the round-1 screenshot were bench players or part of a larger squad.
whatThisChangesInOurDocuments: efl/data/rounds/round-01.json: the graded result is VOIDED back to null, with the faulty grading preserved for reference and the full diagnosis appended. The picks, the lock snapshot and every timestamp are untouched.
scripts/efl/grade-round.mjs: a plausibility guard now refuses to grade when most players show negative round points, and names the season rollover as the likely cause.
Nothing else. No pick, weight or rating moves, and no score is invented for anybody.
